name: HanoiDB
tagline: Pure-Erlang LSM B-tree storage engine from Trifork and Basho, usable as a Riak backend.
description: HanoiDB is an indexed key-value storage engine written in about 2,000 lines of Erlang by Trifork with Basho. Its primary index is an LSM B-tree built from levels that double in size, and merging is done incrementally on every insert, so inserts, deletes and reads have a worst-case O(log2 N) cost without background merge storms. It is append-only with CRC-checked, optionally compressed data, uses Bloom filters to skip disk lookups, supports per-key and global expiry, and gives efficient range scans for Riak secondary indexes; its level visualiser looks like the Towers of Hanoi puzzle. It plugged into Riak through riak_kv_tower_backend. The last commit was in 2016.
statusNote: Unmaintained: no commits since 2016 and Riak has moved on to other backends.
developer: Trifork (Kresten Krab Thorup) with Basho Technologies

scale.notes: Single-node engine; distribution comes from Riak when used as its backend.

strengths: Incremental merging gives predictable worst-case latency
Pure Erlang: no NIFs to crash the BEAM VM
Fast range scans and key listing for Riak 2i
Append-only, checksummed files make crash recovery simple
weaknesses: Slower than native-code engines such as LevelDB for raw throughput
Tied to old Erlang/OTP and Riak versions
useCases: Maintaining old Riak clusters that use the tower backend
notIdealFor: New Erlang or Elixir projects needing active support
